options.explanation: Correct. 12 = 1100, 11 = 1011; bitwise AND keeps only the shared top bit: 1000 = 8. This is x & (x − 1), which clears the lowest set bit of 12.
Bitwise AND can't produce a 1 where 12 has a 0; 11 has bits that 12 doesn't.
0111 = 7 is 12 ^ 11 (XOR), the bits where they differ.

workedExample:
```
12      = 1100
11      = 1011
12 & 11 = 1000  = 8
```

Since 11 = 12 − 1, this is the x & (x − 1) trick: subtracting 1 turned the lowest 1 of 12 (the 4s bit) into 0 and the bits below it into 1s; bitwise AND wipes them all, leaving 1000.
